layout_details.content: ## 24 Advanced concepts
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: To allow effective and error free specification or use of dictionary elements, concepts are provided that support constraining or reuse of already specified properties, grouping, or description of configurable items.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.2 Condition
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In many cases statements or propositions are valid only if additional information is available such as side conditions or initial states. Conditions allow specifying information that has to be known for interpretation of a given value without ambiguities.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A Property may refer to any number of conditions. Conditions represent always additional information. Conditions may again be subject to other conditions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE This document does not provide concepts such as optional conditions or mandatory conditions. Nevertheless preconditions can be expressed. In the example below, the condition "Response time" acts as precondition for the conditions "Melting time" and "Arc quenching time".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Empty conditions, i.e. condition Property information objects without associated value, may exist.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 When specifying the $ I^{2} t_{\mathrm{s}} $ value of a fuse, several side conditions have to be considered (see Figure 27 and Figure 28).

layout_details.content: ## 24.3 Reuse of properties
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Situations occur where Property information objects should be referenced to avoid duplicated concepts.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The attribute is_case_of provides an import of one or more "foreign" properties from another class. It is insignificant whether this class is part of the same class tree or if it resides in another class tree. The imported relations are inherited to subclasses in the same way as relations that are not assigned by is_case_of.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE A class "personal computer" can exist in a class tree "computer" and a class "hard drive" can reside in a tree "memory". To avoid duplication of the Property information objects "disk speed" and "storage capacity", the attribute is_case_of is used. Figure 31 shows the related information objects.

layout_details.content: ## 24.4 Classes and properties for common use
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Classes below the node "Feature class" are a specific type of classes that may be used as readily defined building blocks to provide solutions for frequently occurring use cases, such as specification of address data, tolerance data, environmental conditions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This allows the definition of classes and associated lists of properties which lie outside the classification schema for items, materials, geometry, etc. With this facility, classes can be defined which group together a number of related properties. A link to such classes can then be established by creating a Property with data_type CLASS_INSTANCE_TYPE (see 10.4.4) or CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE (see 10.4.5). This may be done in every class throughout the whole classification hierarchy. The link makes all properties of the referenced class available within the class from which the link is made and, by inheritance, within any of its subclasses.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The example shows how a feature class can be used to create a property of a toleranced capacitance (see Figure 32).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The entry class AAA238 is available for reference from anywhere within the classification hierarchy. As an example, toleranced capacitance could be defined as a property within the subclass for fixed capacitors.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE The reference property can be subject to conditions in the same way as any other property.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The main use of such commonly usable classes is grouping related properties for creation of more complex data types than provided in this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.5 Block
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Blocks are a means to structure properties in a convenient and task related way. By using blocks the properties relevant for an Item_class can be collected and simply reused. Using blocks saves time because blocks can serve as readymade templates and, in addition, blocks help to improve quality by ensuring that an already agreed information set can be reused
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: without unwanted modification. Figure 33 and Figure 34 show the use of Item_class and Property for creating a block.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE See IEC 61987-10:2009 for additional information.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 33 - Interpretation of Class and Property information objects forming a block
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A block consists of an Item_class serving as handle for the block as a whole plus one or more Property information objects that carry the information content of the block. Properties of data type CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE may be part of the Property information objects of a block. Such properties add other blocks to the structure. This nesting of blocks may occur to any depth.

layout_details.content: ## 24.6 Cardinality
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Recurring structures may occur when specifying data structures. Making use of such structures can greatly enhance compactness and clearness of the resulting dictionary. Cardinality allows specifying limits for the creation of occurrences of such structures.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 A bicycle has two similar wheels. To specify the wheels, the creation of a specification for a wheel is sufficient, which then is used two times.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 35 and Figure 36 show the use of Item_class and Property information objects for creating cardinality.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE See IEC 61987-10:2009 for additional information.

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 Figure 36 shows a situation where an aircraft can have between one and four jet engines. The user can specify in the condition (PAA506) the exact number of engines for a specific case, e.g. three. Depending on this number, an application can then create three occurrences of the jet engine description block (CAA203).

layout_details.content: ## 24.7 Polymorphism
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.7.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Devices can largely change their function depending on configuration parameters. Especially devices controlled by software can be configured for executing specific functions out of a set of multiple predefined functions, thus requiring specific (predefined) sets of characteristics for specification.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## NOTE 1 See IEC 61987-10:2009, 4.3.2 for additional information.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Polymorphism structures provide the ability for selecting a block of properties from a predefined set of blocks for specifying the characteristics of a class according to the intended configuration of its class instances. Thus, it can be ensured that the class is always specified by a set of characteristics specifically tailored to the intended use of its instances.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Care should be taken not to create inconsistencies by providing polymorphic choices that contradict the definition of the class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE A measuring device has a communication interface offering the choices of 20 mA communication, wireless communication, or bus communication. By providing a purpose-made block of properties for each communication alternative, the user can select the appropriate specification for his specific configuration.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 37 shows the use of Item_class and Property information objects for creating a polymorphism.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [SOURCE: IEC 61987-10:2009, Figure 6]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 37 - Interpretation of Class and Property information objects forming a polymorphism
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.7.2 Polymorphic choices directly assigned to the specified Item_class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The polymorphic choices to choose from are linked to an Item_class using pointers, i.e. Property information objects, with property_data_element_type = CLASS_REFERENCE_TYPE. These pointers are restricted by a condition enumerating the allowed choices. The wording used within the Value information objects and the preferred_name attributes of the Item_class information objects of the polymorphic choices shall be identical (see Figure 38).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: These polymorphic choices may carry clear text names, such as "Aqueous phase".

layout_details.content: ## 24.8 Relation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.8.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Relation is a powerful means to link instances in dictionaries specifying sub-collections of information objects. Depending on the content of the attributes relation_type and role_of_the_relation, the following cases may be expressed:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) constraint on one or more properties, as an extension of a single property constraint;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) grouping among ontological entities, in particular among heterogeneous ones;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) mapping, correspondence, or transition among ontological entities.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Cases a) and b) are explained in greater detail in 24.8.2 and 24.8.3, respectively.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 24.8.2 Restricted enumeration
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Predefined enumerations (i.e. value lists) avoid selection of wrong or meaningless choices as values for properties. It is strongly recommended to apply existing standardized enumerations providing in most cases exhaustive lists of values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: However, in some cases there is a requirement for narrowing the choices offered.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE A given enumeration provides all colours that can be delivered as colour of a specific sort of glass. If the intended use of the glass is to be the shield of a traffic light, it can be desirable to restrict the enumeration of deliverable colours to the three colours that are foreseen for traffic lights (red, yellow, and green). Figure 40 shows the example.

layout_details.content: ## 24.8.3 Grouping
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Besides the grouping of objects in hierarchies, another type of grouping can be desirable.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The example below shows the use of Relation information objects for creating special predefined lists of units. In general, predefined lists of units offer a selection of units for users that can minimize erroneous choices. In cases where the offered list is too bulky containing units that are not appropriate, the possible selections have to be restricted thus achieving meaningful choices (see Figure 41 and Figure 42).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE To specify the gap of a labyrinth seal, units such as metre (m), millimetre (mm), or micrometre ( $ \mu $ m) can apply. By specifying a list of units embracing m, mm, and $ \mu $ m, absurd length measures such as kilometre (km) or nanometre (nm) can be excluded.

layout_details.content: ## 25 Qualifiers
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: There are cases where users want to add additional information to the values assigned to a property. This information contains data required for the correct interpretation of the value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE A property can be used along the life cycle of a product and its value can depend on the life-cycle stage. Thus, assigning the life-cycle stage to the property value is essential for the correct interpretation of the value. The value associated during the stage "as designed" can well differ from the value during the stage "as built".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The additional information is contained in so-called (value-)qualifiers and may be specified using the rules of this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 See IEC 62569-1 for additional information.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Qualifiers shall not be confused with conditions. Conditions apply to all possible values of a Property whereas qualifiers are strictly related to identified value(s) of a Property.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The same value may be applied with one or more qualifiers. When assigning another value to the Property the qualifiers can change.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Association of qualifiers to values is not an activity performed in a dictionary but is performed by application software. By providing qualifier objects in the dictionary the application software can select from predefined, standardized names for qualifiers. Such qualifiers can provide information such as status data or life-cycle data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26 Characters and character sets
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Characters and character sets play an important role in supporting the versatility and usability of a dictionary. Thus, efforts should be made to equally support European and non-European character sets.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26.2 Recommended character sets
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Unicode characters that correspond to the G0 set of ISO/IEC 646 or to row 00, columns 002 to 007 of ISO/IEC 10646, UTF-16 shall be used for any textual or numerical information.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For alternative languages or missing characters such as " $ \vartheta $ " (GREEK THETA SYMBOL), the full character set as defined by ISO/IEC 10646 may be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The character "9" (GREEK THETA SYMBOL) can be expressed by using the Unicode coding "U+03D1".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 The Unicode standard is published by The Unicode Consortium, P.O. Box 391476, Mountain View, CA 94039-1476, U.S.A., www.unicode.org.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Characters from ISO/IEC 10646 shall be represented by their 4 digit hexadecimal identifier preceded by a number sign "#" character. A number sign "#" not followed by a number shall not be interpreted as the start of a Unicode hexadecimal identifier.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE " $ \oslash $ " is coded as " #2205 "
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26.3 Line feed
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Many applications do not support the use of line feed characters as part of a value. The vertical line "|" character may be used instead.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Two consecutive vertical line characters "||" do not mean double line feed but create a single vertical line "|".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26.4 Subscript
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Subscripts shall be indicated by Latin letter(s) preceded by an underline "_" character followed by a closing curly bracket "}" after the subscript.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An underline " _ " not followed by a closing curly bracket shall not be interpreted as subscript command.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 "λ<sub>peak</sub>" is coded as "$l_peak$".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Non-character subscript glyphs such as subscript numbers can be presented by using Unicode characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 "H $ _{2} $ SO $ _{4} $ " can be presented by writing "H#2082SO#2084".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26.5 Superscript
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Superscripts shall be indicated by Latin letter(s) preceded by two asterisk characters "**" followed by a closing curly bracket "}" after the superscript.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Two asterisks "**" not followed by a closing curly bracket shall not be interpreted as superscript command.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 "αⁿ" is coded as "$a**b"".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Non-character superscript glyphs such as superscript numbers can be presented by using Unicode characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 "10 $ ^{-3} $ " can be presented by writing "10#207B#00B3".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 26.6 Greek characters
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: To express Greek characters the transliteration specified in Table 7 (Table 1 of ISO 843:1997) may be used. For retranslation, the translated Greek letters shall be preceded by a dollar "$" character.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The character "$" not followed by one of the characters specified in Table 7 shall not be interpreted as transliteration command.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 Table 7 is only to express quantities, not to transliterate into New Greek writing.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 See 26.2 for recommendations about use of Unicode characters.

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Type classification codes of properties
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1 Property classification
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1.1 Overview
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Property information objects should be classified in order to make large collections of properties more manageable. This may be implemented by dividing the subject field from the generic to the specific, bringing related concepts together (e.g. concepts referring to the same physical quantity such as temperature, voltage, capacitance) and thus making orientation easier. The field of interest can be divided into a number of classes which should be complementary, i.e. in the ideal case they cover in their totality the whole field without overlap.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The classification supports tasks such as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - analysing property collections;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - designating properties;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - managing properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1.2 Principles
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: There shall be two general categories of Property information objects:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - quantitative properties, also called measures, representing the values of a measurable characteristic of an item. These Property information objects shall be part of the main classes "C", "E", etc.;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - non-quantitative properties such as identifiers or indicators labelling objects or designating items. The non-quantitative Property information objects shall be implemented by means of codes, names, descriptions, etc. Such Property information objects belong to main class "A".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1.3 Quantitative Property information objects
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The quantitative Property information objects shall be classified into main classes according to their measure concepts or quantities in accordance with Table B.1.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Table B.1 - Survey of main classes of Property information objects
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The classification of properties uses the following general rules.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The classification shall have two levels:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - main classes;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - classes identified by a single capital letter and two numeric digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) The main classes, except class J, reflect main areas of physics, such as space and time, mechanics, heat, etc.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) The main classes are subdivided into classes of physical quantities such as T10: velocity, K01: mass, H12: thermal resistance.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) The main class J shall be subdivided into classes based on definitions from the ISO 2382 series.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In addition the following rules apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) For quantities occurring in various physical domains, their complete physical context shall be decisive for the classification.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 Wavelengths of light and sound are classified in class L03 or G05, respectively.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) ISO classes containing a physical constant shall not be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 E32/ L06: speed of light, L18: Stefan-Boltzmann constant.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: g) Dimensionless ratios of identical quantities, expressed as fractions or percentages and not contained in Annex B, shall be classified in the same class as the quantity from which they originate.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 Current gain of a transistor is classified as E01.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: h) Derived quantities shall be classified in the class of the numerator.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 4 Steepness of a voltage pulse (in V/s) in class E06.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1.4 Non-quantitative Property information objects
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The values of non-quantitative properties represent identifiers or designators of items such as locations, organizations, persons, messages, documents, etc. As a result, these Property information objects belong to the main class "A" and may be further classified according to their subject, identified by two additional numeric digits.

layout_details.content: ## Annex E (informative)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Classifying_data_element_type attribute
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A classifying_data_element_type attribute has a value domain consisting of a value list containing at least two options. Its principal function, when associated with an Item_class, is to provide a list of that class' subclasses. Thus, in the IEC dictionary, all classes except for those at the ends of branches of the classification tree have an associated classifying_data_element_type, which is one of the attributes applicable to that class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of the classifying_data_element_type is supported in the information model of IEC 61360-2 and is a mandatory requirement of IEC 61360-1, though some dictionaries currently under development using the same information model have chosen not to take advantage of the facility.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In this document, there is a requirement that the coded_name of a subclass shall be identical to one of the value codes in the value list of its super-class, but this requirement is not included in the information model of IEC 61360-2. It is also desirable that the preferred_name of a subclass be the same as the value meaning associated with the corresponding value code, but this not a requirement of either this document or IEC 61360-2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Annex F (informative)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Conventions for names and definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.1 Conventions for writing definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.1.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Clause F.1 provides guidance on the wording of definitions. Subclauses F.1.2 and F.1.3 give a high-level overview of the conventions for writing definitions as laid down in ISO/IEC 11179-4 and ISO 704, respectively.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.1.2.1 Requirements
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A definition shall:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) be stated in the singular;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) state what the concept is, not what it is not;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) be stated as one descriptive phrase or sentence;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) contain only commonly understood abbreviations;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) be expressed without embedding definitions of other data or underlying concepts.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.1.2.2 Recommendations
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A definition should:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) state the essential meaning of the concept;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) be precise and unambiguous;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) be concise;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) be able to stand alone;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) be expressed without embedding rationale, functional usage, or procedural information;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) avoid circular reasoning;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: g) use the same terminology and consistent logical structure for related definitions;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: h) be appropriate for the type of data being defined.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) Define what it is, not what it is not.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Define the concept, do not write a list of examples (extensional definitions, i.e. a list of subordinate concepts, are allowed in highly specialized domains only).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) Avoid circular definitions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) Do not define two concepts. A definition shall describe only one concept. It shall not include hidden definitions for any concepts used to identify characteristics. Any characteristic that requires an explanation shall be defined separately as a concept or given in a note.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) A definition is valid if it can replace a designation in a text without loss of or change in meaning.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) Definitions shall be as brief as possible and as complex as necessary. Complex definitions can contain several dependent clauses, but carefully written definitions contain only that information which makes the concept unique. Any additional descriptive information deemed necessary should be included in a note.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: g) The definition should not contain characteristics that belong logically to superordinate or subordinate concepts.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: h) A definition shall describe the content of the concept precisely. It shall be neither too narrow nor too broad.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.1.4 Additional conventions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) The term "value" shall not be written in plural even if it is a level type (e.g. minimum, typical and maximum value).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) Changing attributes to conform to the new conventions of this document is by default a revision change (minor change) unless specified otherwise, and is done along with a change request associated with the relevant classes or properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.2 Conventions for writing names
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.2.1 Requirements
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A dictionary item name shall:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) be stated in the singular;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) be written in lower case with the exception of particular abbreviations and acronyms that are commonly written in upper case and approved for use;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) contain only commonly understood abbreviations and acronyms;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) be consistent with the concept specified in the definition.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The name ought not include the term "continuous" in the property name attribute if "continuous" is not addressed in its definition.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.2.2 Recommendations
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A dictionary item name should:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) be concise;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) use the same terminology and consistent logical structure for related names.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.2.3 Mechanical quantitative property names
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Mechanical quantitative property names should start with the concept or item being specified followed by the measured aspect such as length, height, or diameter.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.2.4 Electrical quantitative property names
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) They should reflect the electrical symbol in words reading in reverse order.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) They should start with the concept being specified, followed by the characterized quantity such as voltage, current, capacitance, or temperature.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) They should use the term "repetitive" as part of the name, when defined as such in the symbol:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - "repetitive" in symbol as subscript "R" (e.g. VRRM, Repetitive peak reverse voltage), "non-repetitive" in symbol as subscript "S" (e.g. VRSM, Surge reverse voltage). Do not use the term "single pulse".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Include "repetitive" and "non-repetitive" in primary property name and the definition.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: "Repetitive" should not be used instead of "pulsed". Pulsed does not indicate if it is repetitive or non-repetitive.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) The concept may be preceded by one or more qualifiers such as maximum, peak average, or total.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) The measured quantity is possibly followed by a non-quantitative condition such as: "from junction to lead".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: f) For limiting values, names should be chosen that include the term "limiting" at the beginning.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE See Table F.1 for a name structure for electrical quantitative properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## F.2.5 Non-quantitative property names
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Non-quantitative property names start with the concept being specified followed by a qualifier such as type, code, name, or description.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Annex G (normative)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Value format specification
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO 13584-42 and IEC 61360-2 provide a particular syntax to specify the allowed formats for the string and numeric values that may be associated with a property.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The format description language defined here is based on stipulations given in ISO 6093:1985 and ISO 9735-1:2002.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 The format NR1..3 allows to specify that only integer values consisting of exactly three digits are allowed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 No value format is defined for any other data_type, including boolean_type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 In ISO 13584-42, it is not mandatory to define the format of property values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 The syntax of the allowed formats is defined in Annex G using a subset of the Extended Backus-Naur Form (EBNF) defined in ISO/IEC 14977.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 The syntax of the format NR1 3 are the characters 'NR1' ' ' '3'.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The semantics of the characters used to represent a value cannot be defined using the EBNF. Thus the meaning is specified separately for each part of the format.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 The syntax of the format "NR1 3" has the following meaning: "NR1" means that only an integer value may be represented. The space means that this format specifies a fixed number of characters. "3" means that exactly three digits are required.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.2 Notation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Table G.1 summarizes the subset of the ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF syntactic meta-language used by ISO 13584-42 / IEC 61360-2 specifying the value format of properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Using these notations, the syntax of the subset of the EBNF meta-language used by ISO 13584-42 / IEC 61360-2 to specify the value format of properties is summarized by the following grammar (the meta-identifier character, letter and digit are not detailed):
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: The equals sign '=' indicates a syntax rule. The meta-identifier on the left may be re-written by the combination of the elements on the right. Any spaces appearing between the elements are meaningless unless they appear within a terminal. A syntax rule is terminated by a semicolon ';'.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of a meta-identifier within a definition-list denotes a non-terminal symbol which appears on the left side of another syntax rule. A meta-identifier is composed of letters or digits, the first character being a letter. If a term contains both a primary preceding a minus sign, and a primary that follows the minus sign, only the sequence of symbols that are represented by the first primary and that are not represented by the second primary are represented by the term.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 The notation "" , character - "" , "" means any character but the apostrophe character, inserted between two apostrophe characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The terminal denotes a symbol which cannot be expanded further by a syntax rule, and which appears in the final result. Two ways to represent a terminal are allowed: either a set of characters without apostrophe, inserted between two apostrophes, or a set of characters without quotation marks, inserted between two quotation marks.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 Assume that we want to describe, by such a grammar, the price of a product in euros. Such a price is a positive number with no more than two digits in the cents part. We introduce three meta-identifiers associated with three syntax rules:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: With these syntax rules, "012", "4323.3", "3.56" are examples of permitted representations of euros. "12.", ".10" are examples of not permitted representations of euros.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.3 Data value format types
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The grammar defined in Annex G defines eight different types of value formats: four quantitative and five non-quantitative value formats.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Clause G.4 defines the meta-identifiers that are used to specify these formats. Clause G.5 defines the syntax rule for the four meta-identifiers that represent the four quantitative value formats, together with their meaning at the value level. Clause G.6 defines the meta-identifiers for the five non-quantitative value formats, together with their meaning at the value level.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.4 Meta-identifier used to define the formats
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meta-identifiers used in the grammar that define the various value formats are the following:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: If a number comprises only one digit, no trailing Digit is present.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.5 Quantitative value formats
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.5.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The four quantitative value format syntax rules and their meanings for value representation are defined in G.5.2 to G.5.5.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.5.2 NR1-value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NR1-value syntax specifies the format of an integer property value.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: The meaning of NR1-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'NR1': the value shall be an integer. NR1-values shall not contain any spaces.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfNumber: number of digits of the value. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - signedNumber: if signedNumber is present, the related number shall have either a positive, negative, or zero value. In case of positive values, a '+' sign may be present. Negative values shall be preceded by a '-' sign. The value zero shall not be preceded by a '-' sign.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the related number shall contain a number of digits that is less than or equal to its length specification, i.e. less than or equal to lengthOfNumber.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.5.3 NR2-value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NR2-value syntax specifies the format of a real property value that does not need an exponent.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR2Value = 'NR2', ((signedNumber, variableLengthIndicator) | (signedNumber, space) | variableLengthIndicator | space), lengthOfIntegralPart, decimalMark, lengthOfFractionalPart;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of NR2-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'NR2': the value shall be a real number. NR2-values shall not contain spaces.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfFractionalPart: number of digits of the fractional part of the number. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the fractional part may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE lengthOfFractionalPart implicitly specifies the recommended accuracy of the value. The actual accuracy of the number from which this value was derived can have been greater than the value expressed here.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfIntegralPart: number of digits of the integral part of the number. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the integral part may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - signedNumber: if signedNumber is present, the related number shall have either a positive, negative, or zero value. In case of positive values a '+' sign may be present. Negative values shall be preceded by a '-' sign. The value zero shall not be preceded by a '-' sign.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, either integral part or fractional part of the number or both parts shall contain a number of digits that is less than or equal to its related length specification, i.e. less than or equal to lengthOfIntegralPart or lengthOfFractionalPart. At least one cipher shall be present in the number.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.5.4 NR3-value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NR3-value syntax specifies the format of a real property value that is represented with an exponent.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR3Value = 'NR3'，((signedNumber, variableLengthIndicator) | (signedNumber, space) | variableLengthIndicator | space),
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: lengthOfIntegralPart, decimalMark, lengthOfFractionalPart exponentIndicator, [signedExponent], lengthOfExponent;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of NR3-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'NR3': the value shall be a real number with an exponent of base 10. There shall be at least one digit and the decimal mark in the mantissa. The exponent shall contain at least one digit, too. NR3-values shall not contain spaces.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - exponentIndicator: separator between mantissa and exponent in numbers of format NR3.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfExponent: number of digits of the exponent. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the exponent may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 Any signs or decimal marks present are not counted by lengthOfNumber, lengthOfIntegralPart, lengthOfFractionalPart or lengthOfExponent.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfFractionalPart: number of digits of the fractional part of the mantissa. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the fractional part may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 lengthOfFractionalPart implicitly specifies the recommended accuracy of the value. The actual accuracy of the number from which this value was derived can have been greater than the value expressed here.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfIntegralPart: number of digits of the integral part of the mantissa. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the integral part may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - signedExponent: if signedExponent is present, the related exponent shall have either a positive, negative, or zero value. In case of positive values, a '+' sign may be present. Negative values shall be preceded by a '-' sign. The value zero shall not be preceded by a '-' sign.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the related number or exponent shall contain a number of digits that is less than or equal to its related length specification, i.e. less than or equal to lengthOfIntegralPart, lengthOfFractionalPart, or lengthOfExponent. At least one cipher shall be present in the mantissa and in the exponent.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.5.5 NR4-value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NR4-value syntax specifies the format of a rational property value that is presented with an integer part or a fraction part with a denominator and a numerator.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NR4Value = 'NR4', ((signedNumber, variableLengthIndicator) | (signedNumber, space) | variableLengthIndicator | space), lengthOfIntegerPart, numeratorIndicator, lengthOfNumerator, denominatorIndicator, lengthOfDenominator;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of NR4-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'NR4': the value shall be a rational number represented either as an integer, or as a fraction consisting of a numerator and a denominator. There shall be at least one digit either in the integer part, or both in the numerator and in the denominator part. If one part of the fraction contains a digit, the other part shall also contain some digits. NR4 number values shall not contain any spaces.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 12 and $ ^{3 / 4} $ are valid numbers that can be presented in the NR4 format. $ 12^{3 / 4} $ is not a valid presentation.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - numeratorIndicator: separator between the integer part description and the fraction part description in NR4 formats.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfNumerator: number of digits of the numerator. If the value of the rational number is completely represented by its integer part, neither the numerator of the fraction nor its denominator shall be represented. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the numerator may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - denominatorIndicator: separator between the numerator part description and the denominator part description in NR4 formats.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfDenominator: number of digits of the denominator. If the value of the rational number is completely represented by its integer part, neither the numerator of the fraction nor its denominator shall be represented. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the denominator may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - lengthOfIntegerPart: number of digits of the integer part of the rational number. If preceded by a variableLengthIndicator the actual number of digits of the denominator may be less.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the three parts of the rational number shall contain a number of digits that is less than or equal to its related length specification, i.e. less than or equal to lengthOfIntegralPart, lengthOfNumerator, or lengthOfDenominator. At least one cipher shall be present either in the integral part, or in the two parts of the fraction.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6 Non-quantitative value formats
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The five non-quantitative value format syntax rules and their meanings are defined in G.6.2 to G.6.6.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 For translatable_string_type the value format applies to any language-specific representation of the string.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 For non_quantitative_code_type, the value format applies to the code.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Non-quantitative values are represented by strings which comprise characters. The length of a string may be either specified by directly specifying the upper limit of the number of contained characters or by specifying that the total number of characters may be any integral multiple of the length specified.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: The meaning of the factor components is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - factor: when factor is present, then numberOfCharacters shall be any integral multiple of the value given in factor. factor shall not contain the value zero.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - numberOfCharacters: determines the maximum number of characters contained in the string.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6.2 Alphabetic value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An "Alphabetic value format (A)" defines the value format of a string that contains alphabetic letters. Thus, the content shall be taken from the characters of row 00, cell 20, cells 40 to 7E, or cells C0 to FF, of the Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP) (Plane 00 of Group 00) of ISO/IEC 10646. Due to potential interpretation problems of value content within components of one system or of multiple systems, where possible, the characters used should be restricted to the G0 set of ISO/IEC 646 or to row 00, columns 002 to 007 of ISO/IEC 10646.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE For alternative languages, as supported by translated data, the relevant characters or ideographs of the related language-specific character set are available as defined by the Unicode Standard. In some cases, there is no 1:1 relation between the characters of the source language and the characters of the target language.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE CJK (Chinese-Japanese-Korean) ideographs.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: AValue = 'A', (space | variableLengthIndicator), numberOfCharacters;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of A-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'A': the value shall be a string, or several substrings, of alphabetic letters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the string may contain fewer characters than indicated by numberOfCharacters. The string shall contain at least one character.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6.3 Mixed characters value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A "Mixed characters value format (M)" format defines the value format of a string that may contain any character specified in Clause 26.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE For alternative languages as supported by translated data, the relevant characters or ideographs of the related language-specific character set are available as defined by the Unicode Standard.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE CJK (Chinese-Japanese-Korean) characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: MValue = 'M', (space | variableLengthIndicator), numberOfCharacters;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of M-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'M': the value shall be a string, or several substrings.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the string may contain fewer characters than indicated by numberOfCharacters. The string shall contain at least one character.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6.4 Number value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A "Number value format (N)" defines the value format of a string that contains numeric digits only. Thus, the content shall be taken from the characters of row 00, cell 2B, cell 2D, cells 30 to 39, or cell 45 of the Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP) (Plane 00 of Group 00) of ISO/IEC 10646.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE For alternative languages as supported by translated data, the relevant characters or ideographs of the related language-specific character set are available as defined by the Unicode Standard.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Table G.2 shows the transposition of the European digits "0" to "9" into Arabic digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Table G.2 - Transposing European style digits into Arabic digits
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
European digits9876543210
Arabic digits9AV70ε۳۳۱.
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: ## Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NValue = 'N', (space | variableLengthIndicator), numberOfCharacters;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of N-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'N': the value shall be a string, or several substrings, of numeric digits.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the string may contain fewer characters than indicated by numberOfCharacters. The string shall contain at least one character.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6.5 Mixed alphabetic or numeric characters value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A "Mixed alphabetic or numeric characters value format (X)" defines the value format of a string that contains alphanumeric characters, i.e. any combination of characters from A-value format or N-value format.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE For alternative languages as supported by translated data, the relevant characters or ideographs of the related language-specific character set are available as defined by the Unicode Standard.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: XValue = 'X', (space | variableLengthIndicator), numberOfCharacters;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of X-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'X': the value shall be a string, or several substrings, of alphanumeric, i.e. any combination of alphabetic and numeric, characters.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the string may contain fewer characters than indicated by numberOfCharacters. The string shall contain at least one character.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.6.6 Binary value format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A "Binary value format (B)" defines the value format of a string that contains binary characters, i.e. "0" or "1". Thus the content shall be taken from the characters of row 00, cell 30 or 31, of the Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP) (Plane 00 of Group 00) of ISO/IEC 10646.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE For alternative languages as supported by translated data, the relevant characters or ideographs of the related language-specific character set are available as defined by the Unicode Standard.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: BValue = 'B', (space | variableLengthIndicator), numberOfCharacters;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The meaning of B-value format components for value representation is as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - 'B': the value shall be a string, or several substrings, consisting of binary values, i.e. the characters "0" or "1" or sequences thereof.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - variableLengthIndicator: if variableLengthIndicator is present, the string may contain fewer characters than indicated by numberOfCharacters. The string shall contain at least one character.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## G.7 HTML5 format
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In cases where values have to be presented in a non-numerical form, e.g. as a mathematical formula or in pictorial form, HTML5 (see W3C Recommendation 28:2014) may be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE In case of three phase electrical systems, numeric values are often presented as multiples of $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} $ or
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Syntax rule:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Html5Value = 'HTML5';
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Table G.3 contains some examples for values that may be contained in numbers and strings characterized by the above value format scheme.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Annex H (informative)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Modelling notation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## H.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For specifying the data model of this document, class diagrams of Unified Modelling Language (UML) are used. Clauses H.2 to H.5 give a short introduction of the utilized UML constructs. For a detailed description see ISO/IEC 19505-1.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## H.2 UML Class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The UML class diagrams in Figure H.1 to Figure H.3 show the concepts used to model the information objects, their attributes and relationships.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE An IEC 61360-1 concept can comprise more than one UML class information object.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: UML classes have attributes specifying their characteristics. Relationships between the classes reveal how they are structured in terms of each other. Classes are related in a variety of ways, as described in Clauses H.3 to H.5.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## H.3 Generalization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A generalization is a relationship between a general class (superclass) and a specific class (subclass). A generalization provides for the subclass to inherit all information including relationships from the superclass. Since a subtype inherits all the characteristics from its superclass, the subclass shall specify only the additional information as characteristics.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure H.1 - Example for generalization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure H.1 is an example of generalization. In this example Relation is a more specific type of Dictionary_element. Relation inherits all attributes and associations from Dictionary_element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 The UML class "Relation" in Figure H.1 is a subtype of the UML_class "Dictionary_element".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Abstract supertypes have a name which is written in italics.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 The UML class "Dictionary_element" in Figure H.1 is an abstract supertype.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## H.4 Simple association
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An association is a conceptual connection between classes. Each association has two "association ends". Each association end describes the role the target class (i.e. the class the association end goes to) has in relation to the source class (i.e. the class the association end
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: comes from). Each association end has cardinality (multiplicity), which specifies the number of information objects that may participate in the given relationship.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Figure H.2 shows a case where the UML class "Property" has an optional reference to a UML class "Drawing".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure H.2 - Example of an association
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In this example, a Property information object may refer to zero or one Drawing information objects whereas any Drawing may be referenced by zero, one or many Property information objects.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE An asterisk "*" stands for "any number". If no cardinality is specified "any number (*)" is assumed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## H.5 Modularization with UML package
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For a better overview the UML model was split into modules. Each of these can easily be presented on a single page. For implementation of the modularization the UML construct "package" was used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A package is a collection of UML elements that can be used for dividing a UML model into smaller, better manageable parts. Almost all UML elements can be grouped into UML packages. Each package establishes an own namespace for its members. A namespace may import elements from other namespaces. If a member of a namespace with the name N is an element with the name x, then the member can be referred to by a qualified name of the form "N::x".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Figure H.3 shows a case where the UML class "Item_class" references the UML class "Value_list", which is owned by the UML package "Value_list_concept".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure H.3 - Example of an association to a UML class owned by another UML package
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In this document, UML packages are used for grouping UML elements. Thus the model is organized in modules and a more clear presentation of its elements becomes possible. Figure H.4 shows the modules used in this document.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure H.4 - Division of the IEC 61360-1 model into modules
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## AVANT-PROPOS
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 1) La Commission Electrotechnique Internationale (IEC) est une organisation mondiale de normalisation composée de l'ensemble des comités électrotechniques nationaux (Comités nationaux de l'IEC). L'IEC a pour objet de favoriser la coopération internationale pour toutes les questions de normalisation dans les domaines de l'électricité et de l'électronique. A cet effet, l'IEC – entre autres activités – publie des Normes internationales, des Spécifications techniques, des Rapports techniques, des Spécifications accessibles au public (PAS) et des Guides (ci-après dénommés "Publication(s) de l'IEC"). Leur élaboration est confiée à des comités d'études, aux travaux desquels tout Comité national intéressé par le sujet traité peut participer. Les organisations internationales, gouvernementales et non gouvernementales, en liaison avec l'IEC, participent également aux travaux. L'IEC collabore étroitement avec l'Organisation Internationale de Normalisation (ISO), selon des conditions fixées par accord entre les deux organisations.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 2) Les décisions ou accords officiels de l'IEC concernant les questions techniques représentent, dans la mesure du possible, un accord international sur les sujets étudiés, étant donné que les Comités nationaux de l'IEC intéressés sont représentés dans chaque comité d'études.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 3) Les Publications de l'IEC se présentent sous la forme de recommandations internationales et sont agréées comme telles par les Comités nationaux de l'IEC. Tous les efforts raisonnables sont entrepris afin que l'IEC s'assure de l'exactitude du contenu technique de ses publications; l'IEC ne peut pas être tenue responsable de l'éventuelle mauvaise utilisation ou interprétation qui en est faite par un quelconque utilisateur final.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 4) Dans le but d'encourager l'uniformité internationale, les Comités nationaux de l'IEC s'engagent, dans toute la mesure possible, à appliquer de façon transparente les Publications de l'IEC dans leurs publications nationales et régionales. Toutes divergences entre toutes Publications de l'IEC et toutes publications nationales ou régionales correspondantes doivent être indiquées en termes clairs dans ces dernières.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 5) L'IEC elle-même ne fournit aucune attestation de conformité. Des organismes de certification indépendants fournissent des services d'évaluation de conformité et, dans certains secteurs, accèdent aux marques de conformité de l'IEC. L'IEC n'est responsable d'aucun des services effectués par les organismes de certification indépendants.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 6) Tous les utilisateurs doivent s'assurer qu'ils sont en possession de la dernière édition de cette publication.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 7) Aucune responsabilité ne doit être imputée à l'IEC, à ses administrateurs, employés, auxiliaires ou mandataires, y compris ses experts particuliers et les membres de ses comités d'études et des Comités nationaux de l'IEC, pour tout préjudice causé en cas de dommages corporels et matériels, ou de tout autre dommage de quelque nature que ce soit, directe ou indirecte, ou pour supporter les coûts (y compris les frais de justice) et les dépenses découlant de la publication ou de l'utilisation de cette Publication de l'IEC ou de toute autre Publication de l'IEC, ou au crédit qui lui est accordé.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 8) L'attention est attirée sur les références normatives citées dans cette publication. L'utilisation de publications référencées est obligatoire pour une application correcte de la présente publication.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 9) L'attention est attirée sur le fait que certains des éléments de la présente Publication de l'IEC peuvent faire l'objet de droits de brevet. L'IEC ne saurait être tenue pour responsable de ne pas avoir identifié de tels droits de brevets et de ne pas avoir signalé leur existence.

layout_details.content: La Norme internationale IEC 61360-1 a été établie par le sous-comité 3D, Propriétés et classes de produits et leur identification, du comité d'études 3 de l'IEC: Structures d'informations, documentation et symboles graphiques.

layout_details.content: # INTRODUCTION
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: La série IEC 61360 dans son entier spécifie un dictionnaire à usage général de termes techniques couvrant le domaine de l'électrotechnologie, de l'électronique, ainsi que d'autres domaines associés. Le dictionnaire est spécifié sous forme informatique en tant que dictionnaire de référence. Grâce au dictionnaire, les applications peuvent interagir et partager des données de manière non ambiguë et exempte d'incertitudes sémantiques.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Le présent document s'adresse aux ingénieurs et fournit une présentation détaillée de la structure du dictionnaire et de ses usages du point de vue du fournisseur du dictionnaire ainsi que du point de vue de l'utilisateur du dictionnaire. L'IEC 61360-2 spécifie le modèle de données détaillé du dictionnaire et l'IEC 61360-6 stipule les critères de qualité pour le contenu du dictionnaire.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: La référence à un dictionnaire commun est avantageuse dans tous les cas où les informations sur les produits doivent être transférées de manière non ambiguë. Les cas d'usage comprennent des catalogues, des processus de classement, des informations de produits, contenus dans des spécifications ou des contrats.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: La Commission Electrotechnique Internationale a défini un dictionnaire technique destiné à être utilisé dans les domaines électrotechnique et électronique, tenu à jour par le souscomité 3D. Ce dictionnaire est appelé le Dictionnaire de données commun de l'IEC (IEC CDD, Common Data Dictionary) et peut être consulté sur la page web de l'IEC (http://std.iec.ch/iec61360).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Il convient de ne pas confondre les dictionnaires et les catalogues ou les collections de données maîtres; ceux-ci utilisent les objets du dictionnaire. Dans les catalogues ou les collections de données maîtres, les valeurs sont assignées à des instances d'objets du dictionnaire. Ils sont donc construits d'après les dictionnaires. Par conséquent, les dictionnaires sont normalement échangés avant tout catalogue ou collection de données maîtres.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: L'IEC 61360-2 est étroitement associée au présent document. L'IEC 61360-2 contient le modèle d'information utilisant le langage de modélisation EXPRESS. Dans ce modèle, la définition et la structure de l'IEC 61360-1 sont formalisées et présentées sous une forme interprétable par ordinateur.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Le présent document est en grande partie conforme à l'IEC 61360-2:2012 et à l'ISO 13584-42:2010. Cependant, l'usage pratique a montré la nécessité d'étendre le modele de données de façon sélective. La présente quatrième édition de l'IEC 61360-1 complète donc l'IEC 61360-2 en sémantique comme en syntaxe et introduit des constructions supplémentaires disponibles dans l'IEC 62656-1 pour des avantages pratiques. Par exemple, les constructions telles que les énumérations de nombres réels ou les objets d'association n'existent pas dans l'IEC 61360-2 mais sont nécessaires dans de nombreux domaines techniques.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: L'IEC 62656-1 offre des interfaces avec l'IEC CDD. Les demandes de modifications de l'IEC CDD doivent donc être formées conformément à la spécification de l'interface disponible dans cette dernière norme.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Dans certains cas, il peut être difficile de savoir si les mots représentent les noms d'objets d'information ou s'ils traitent simplement d'articles ordinaires, comme pour le terme «propriété».
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Pour cette raison, les règles typographiques suivantes sont utilisées dans le présent document:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - gras et première lettre majuscule: nom d'une classe UML, p. ex. «Propriété»;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - gras et première lettre minuscule: nom d'un attribut UML ou d'une association UML, p. ex. 《numéro_de_révision》;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - police normale (non gras), première lettre minuscule: texte banal, p.ex. «propriété».
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Il convient que les noms d'objets d'information UML soient traités comme des constantes et qu'ils ne soient pas traduits en d'autres langues.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # TYPES NORMALISÉS D'ELÉMENTS DE DONNÉES AVEC PLAN DE CLASSIFICATION -
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Partie 1: Définitions - Principes et méthodes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 1 Domaine d'application
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: La présente partie de l'IEC 61360 spécifie les principes de la définition des propriétés et des attributs associés et explique les méthodes de représentation de concepts définis oralement par des constructions de données appropriées disponibles dans l'IEC 61360-2. Il spécifie également les principes permettant d'établier une hiérarchie de classification à partir d'une collection de classes, dont chacune représente un concept technique d'un domaine électrotechnique ou un domaine relatif à l'électrotechnologie.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: L'utilisation du présent document facilite l'échange des données techniques au moyen d'une structure définie pour l'information à échanger sous une forme interpretable par ordinateur. Chaque propriété à échanger a une signification définie non ambiguë et une dénomination cohérente, le cas échéant un domaine de valeurs défini, un format prescrit et des unités de mesure définies pour toutes les valeurs quantitatives. Des dispositions sont également données pour:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) le contrôle des modifications apportées aux définitions des propriétés par les numéros de version et de révision;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) l'introduction de notes et de remarques pour clarifier et aider à l'application des définitions;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) l'indication des sources des définitions et des listes de valeurs;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) les figures et les formules associées.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Les comités d'études et sous-comités de l'IEC ou d'autres organismes peuvent utiliser le présent document comme une base pour le développement de leurs propres dictionnaires.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Les sujets concernant les infrastructures des technologies de l'information, tels que les exemples qui suivent, ne font pas partie du domaine d'application du présent document:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - sécurité;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - mécanismes de blocage de bases de données;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - gestion des droits d'accès.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## propriété applicable
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: propriété nécessairement détenu par chaque partie membre d'une classe de caractérisation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 à l'article: Chaque partie membre d'une classe de caractérisation possède un aspect correspondant à chaque propriété applicable de cette classe de caractérisation.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 à l'article: La définition ci-dessus est conceptuelle, il n'existe aucune exigence consistant à recommander l'utilisation de toutes les propriétés applicables d'une classe pour décrire chaque partie de cette classe au niveau du modèle de données.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 à l'article: Toutes les propriétés applicables d'une superclasse sont également applicables aux sousclasses de ladite superclasse.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 à l'article: Seules les propriétés définies ou hériées comme visibles et les propriétés importées d'une classe peuvent être des propriétés applicables.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 à l'article: Pour faciliter l'intégration des bibliothèques de composants et des catalogues électroniques basés sur l'ISO 13584-24:2003 et l'ISO 13584-25, ces parties de l'ISO 13584 exigent que seules les propriétés qui sont applicables à une classe soient utilisées pour caractériser leurs instances dans les bibliothèques de composants et les catalogues électroniques.

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: élément de données permettant une description interprétable par ordinateur d'une propriété, d'une relation ou d'une classe

layout_details.content: EXEMPLE Le nom d'une propriété, le code d'une classe, l'unité de mesure dans laquelle sont données les valeurs d'une propriété.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 à l'article: Un attribut ne décrit qu'un seul détail d'une propriété, d'une classe ou d'une relation.

layout_details.content: ## classification

layout_details.content: ## classe

layout_details.content: abstraction d'un ensemble de produits similaires

layout_details.content: Note 1 à l'article: Un produit qui satisfait à l'abstraction définie par une classe est appelé membre de la classe.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 à l'article: Une classe est un concept volontaire pouvant prendre des significations d'extension différentes selon les contextes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXEMPLE L'ensemble de produits utilisés par une entreprise particulière et l'ensemble de tous les produits ISO normalisés sont deux exemples de concepts. Dans ces deux contextes (l'entreprise et l'ISO), l'ensemble des produits qui sont considérés comme membres de la classe roulement à bille unique peuvent être différents, en particulier du fait que les employés de chaque entreprise ignorent le nombre de produits roulements à bille unique existants.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 à l'article: Les classes sont structurées par relations d'inclusion de classe.

layout_details.content: Note 1 à l'article: Les termes «significative au sein d'un domaine d'application d'une classe de caractéristique donnée» signifient qu'un observateur humain peut déterminer, pour tout produit de la classe de caractérisation, si la propriété s'applique et si oui, à quel aspect du produit elle correspond.

Elle peut être définie comme visible au niveau de la vis tout en étant applicable uniquement dans certaines sous-classes.

layout_details.content: Note 3 à l'article: Toutes les propriétés visibles d'une superclasse qui est une classe de caractérisation de produit sont également des propriétés visibles de ses sous-classes.
